event.summary: Retired tmux Python environment becomes unignored without cleanup
event.detail: Reviewed commit: d751ff1633bb479c7bf53920f2e4ea4ba932a1c2. TLDR: An existing checkout with the older tmux build's Python environment can have hundreds of megabytes of generated files swept into its next Jujutsu change when this update stops ignoring that directory. Details: the patch retains .ci-tmux/ specifically because existing checkouts may still hold it and jj tracks new files automatically, but removes the adjacent .ci-tmux-python/ ignore. The previous revision's scripts/build-pinned-tmux-ci.sh:30-33 documents that older versions left about 350 MB at .ci-tmux-python and removes that directory only when that script runs. This commit retires that script, so a checkout upgraded directly from a version that left the environment does not run the cleanup. The leftover environment now becomes ordinary unignored source-tree content. Keeping its ignore alongside the retained .ci-tmux/ entry prevents accidental tracking without requiring execution of retired tooling. Suggested bucket: other (maintainer checkout pollution; no catastrophic route established). Confidence: likely, conditional on a checkout retaining the documented older environment and jj's automatic tracking; no runtime observation or reproduction. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Caveats: a checkout that previously ran the cleanup has no residue and is unaffected; the exact files retained by the old environment were not inspected. Could-be-highest: no established route; the demonstrated concern is accidental tracking and a large generated diff, not user-data destruction or a substantiated credential disclosure.

TLDR: A checkout retaining the older .ci-tmux-python environment can expose generated files to automatic tracking when its root ignore is removed. The earlier claim that the whole roughly 350 MB environment is swept into the next change was too broad: jj has a per-file maximum and other ignore rules may apply. Original suspected consequence preserved but narrowed: accidental generated-file additions and working-copy noise in maintainer tooling, not established blanket tracking of hundreds of megabytes. Source: this commit retains .ci-tmux/ but removes .ci-tmux-python/; its deleted build-pinned-tmux-ci.sh:30-33 documented the older roughly 350 MB environment and explicitly removed it on invocation. No remaining literal reference to ci-tmux-python or tmux-python was found at 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db in scripts, .agents, .github, docs or deflake; the only ci-tmux match is .gitignore:33. Tool-contract checks: installed jj is 0.47.1; jj help file track says new files are automatically tracked by default, snapshot.auto-track defaults to all(), and files exceeding the maximum are not tracked by default. A read-only jj --ignore-working-copy config list --include-defaults snapshot confirms auto-track all() and max-new-file-size 1MiB for this checkout. This limits individual files, not a directory's aggregate size; no reproduction or snapshot was performed. Suggested bucket: other (conditional maintainer checkout pollution, no catastrophic route). Confidence: unverified after investigation for actual leftover inclusion; source-confirmed ignore removal and documented historical residue. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no established security, data-loss or catastrophic route. Exact missing premise: an older retained environment contains files that are neither covered by an internal/other ignore nor over jj's effective per-file size cap. The historical environment creation and any generated internal ignore are being checked next; actual file distribution in an affected checkout has not been inspected. What settles the remaining premise: historical creation contract and, if it varies by Python version, a retained affected environment's file/ignore manifest or an explicit author-supplied account. No live install or other agent's residue was inspected.
